title: pop-tagged bid carries only nurl, no adm at all — a spec-complete bid

source.name: IAB OpenRTB 2.6 §4.3.3 Object:Bid (adm OPTIONAL, nurl the win-notice URL) plus ortbtools' own baseline response completeness check (packages/core/rules-response.js response.bid.payload_missing, which already accepts nurl alone) — the payload is a plain oRTB pop-tagged bid deliberately shipping only the win-notice URL
source.version: repo HEAD at session start, commit a61fc25; IAB 2.6 §4.3.3 (Object:Bid table)
source.license: Internal product code (ortbtools) plus IAB OpenRTB spec citation; no third-party material copied. MIT for the original fixture values.
source.notes: Constructed to isolate the pop-response plugin's independent, stricter demand from Core's own baseline completeness rule.

modifications: All IDs, domains, prices and timestamps independently authored.
device.ip uses TEST-NET 192.0.2.44; user.id is a clearly synthetic string.
advertiser.example.test / tracking.example.test / publisher.example.test are reserved .test hosts; no live host, tracker or subscriber identifier.
provenance.sanitized: No real visitor or subscriber data. IP 192.0.2.44 is TEST-NET-1; every identifier is a synthetic-fixture string; every URL uses a reserved .test hostname.

pairApplicability.note: A genuine oRTB auction pair: the response bid references the offered impression and ids match. The bid deliberately carries no adm, only nurl, to test the win-notice-only completeness path.

device.ua: Mozilla/5.0 (X11; Linux x86_64) AppleWebKit/537.36 (KHTML, like Gecko) Chrome/120.0.0.0 Safari/537.36

specNotes: IAB OpenRTB 2.6 §4.3.3 Object:Bid: `adm` is marked OPTIONAL, and `nurl` (win notice URL, called by the exchange on win) is a documented, independent completeness signal. packages/core/rules-response.js's own baseline check (response.bid.payload_missing) already treats nurl alone as complete — it only WARNs when BOTH adm and nurl are absent.

packages/core/rules/pop-response/index.js's header comment documents exactly three accepted pop adm shapes (bare URL / window.open script / location redirect) and says nothing about nurl as an alternative — its admLooksLikePop check runs on `bid.adm` alone and treats an absent adm the same as an unrecognized adm, regardless of nurl. This is a narrower, INTERNALLY INCONSISTENT contract than Core's own baseline response rule for the exact same bid shape.

A bid this validator itself would accept as complete when the SAME imp had no pop hint (nurl alone, no adm) becomes an ERROR purely because the imp/bid also carries a pop-family ext hint — the pop-response plugin does not special-case a genuinely nurl-only bid.

docs/cu-pops-audit-2026-05-12.md §2/§3 records this exact class of gap as still open ('No validation of bid.nurl for pop win tracking') as of the historical snapshot; this case reproduces it directly against current code.

Preview: nurl/burl are never read by the creative preview path (public/ortbtools.app.js findAdm explicitly skips them) — a nurl-only bid correctly renders the top-level empty state; that part of the contract is not in dispute, only the response-side ERROR is.
notes: Plain `iab` dialect. This case's expectation is deliberately grounded in the spec + Core's own baseline rule, not in the pop-response plugin's stricter behavior — see knownGap DEF-170.

preview.limitation: nurl-only bid has no adm for the preview to render

knownGap.note: packages/core/rules/pop-response/index.js requires bid.adm alone to look like a redirect and does not accept a nurl-only bid, even though Core's own baseline response.bid.payload_missing check (and IAB OpenRTB 2.6 §4.3.3) already treats adm-or-nurl as complete. A pop-tagged bid shipping only nurl is rejected with bid.pop.adm_not_redirect ERROR.
